_help: Rules for Check a message in Spot the Scam. Each rule: id (no spaces), name, category, points, explain (one plain line), and what to match. phrases: words to find, capitals do not matter. patterns: advanced text patterns (regular expressions, backslashes doubled). onlyWith: the rule only counts if the message also has one of these signals: link, payment, urgency, credentials. skipIfNegated: ignore a phrase when 'never', 'no' or similar comes just before it. skipIfAfter: ignore a match when one of these words comes just before it. critical: true jumps the score straight to 100. A few rules have a type that runs a built-in check (links, brands, lookalikes, emojis, capitals, exclamation marks, reported scams); their settings are listed with them. Each rule counts once. The total is capped at 100.

levels.label: Critical
levels.message: Almost certainly a scam. Do not click, reply or connect your wallet.

levels.label: Medium
levels.message: Suspicious. Check through the official app or site, never through this message.

levels.label: Low
levels.message: Few or no red flags matched our rules. That does not mean this message is safe.

_signalsHelp: Signals used by onlyWith. A link is any web address or IP address in the message. The others match these phrases and patterns.

rules.name: Asks for your seed phrase or private key
rules.explain: Anyone with your seed phrase or private key can empty your wallet, and no real company ever asks for it.
patterns: \b(enter|share|send|provide|type|submit|confirm|verify|give|paste|input|write|upload|validate|sync)\b[^.!?\n]{0,40}\b(seed phrase|seed words|recovery phrase|private key|mnemonic|backup phrase|secret phrase|\d{2}[- ]word)

rules.name: Asks you to import a wallet, sign to verify or install a wallet extension
rules.explain: Importing your wallet into a site, signing to 'verify ownership' or installing an unknown extension can hand over control of your funds.

rules.name: Promises free tokens or a reward
rules.explain: Surprise rewards are the most common bait. Real projects announce them on their official site, not in messages.

rules.name: Offers you a coin amount, or mining or payout money
rules.explain: Messages that put a coin amount in front of you, or talk about mining payouts, are trying to make you excited enough to skip the checks.

rules.name: Asks for a fee to unlock or verify
rules.explain: Real rewards never ask you to pay first. The fee is the scam.
phrases: pay the gas fee to claim

rules.name: Fake account alert
rules.explain: Scammers fake alerts about suspended or hacked accounts to rush you onto a fake site. Check your account only in the official app.

rules.name: Asks for a code, password or API key
rules.explain: One-time codes, 2FA codes, passwords and API keys let someone into your account. Never send them to anyone.

rules.name: Paste site or link shortener
rules.explain: Paste sites and shortened links hide where they really go, and scammers use them to dodge filters.

rules.name: Brand name with a link that is not its official site
rules.explain: The link uses a well known name but is not that company's real website, a classic way to copy a login page.

rules.name: Misspelled brand or lookalike characters
rules.explain: A name that is almost right, like binnance or c0inbase, is built to fool a quick glance.

rules.name: Link to a bare IP address
rules.explain: Real companies use named websites. A link made of numbers hides who runs it.

rules.name: Matches a reported scam
rules.explain: This message contains a web address, wallet, email, username, phone number or wording that has been reported as part of a scam.

rules.name: Promises guaranteed or risk free money
rules.explain: Nobody can guarantee returns in crypto. Promises like these are bait.

rules.name: Fee to recover funds or to withdraw
rules.explain: Fund recovery services that charge upfront, and platforms that want a deposit or tax before you can withdraw, are scams.

rules.name: Job or deal that costs you money or control
rules.explain: Real jobs and deals never ask you to deposit crypto, pay a listing fee, or run code or install apps for an interview.
phrases: install the app for the interview

rules.name: Pushes you to a private chat
rules.explain: Moving the conversation to Telegram or WhatsApp takes you away from places where others could warn you.

rules.name: Risky file or locked zip
rules.explain: Program files and password protected zips are how malware gets past email filters onto your computer.

rules.name: Urgent vote, emergency migration or sign to approve
rules.explain: Fake governance alerts rush you into signing approvals that let someone move your tokens.

rules.name: Rushes you
rules.explain: A countdown or deadline is there to stop you from thinking it through.

rules.name: Lots of hype emojis
rules.explain: Rows of hype emojis are typical of mass-sent scam messages.

rules.name: WORDS IN CAPITALS
rules.explain: Shouting in capitals is a cheap way to grab attention, common in scams.

rules.name: Many exclamation marks
rules.explain: Lots of exclamation marks are a sign of hype, not of a real company.

rules.name: Tries to trick AI checkers
rules.explain: Honest messages never contain instructions for AI tools. This text is trying to fool automatic checkers.

example: Hi ✅ https://justpaste.it/hxgfq - 1.34 BTC BINANCE MINING ✅, Enter the OTP Code we sent to your email below to confirm your new password 7880 Expired In: 30 minutes
